name: Venice mints the gold ducat
summary: The Venetian Great Council authorises the minting of the gold ducat (later zecchino), 3.5 g of pure gold matched in weight to the Florentine florin. The ducat becomes the Mediterranean's most stable gold coinage and circulates unchanged in weight and fineness for five centuries.

_quarry.structural_significance: Sets the dominant Mediterranean gold currency standard; carries the Venetian commercial empire into a position of monetary primacy that outlasts its territorial decline.
